headline_marked: Maximum Tk 8,500 set for Class 11 admission; [[fees vary by institution type, location]]
headline: Maximum Tk 8,500 set for Class 11 admission; fees vary by institution type, location
summary: The Ministry of Education has set Class 11 admission fees from Tk 1,500 to Tk 8,500 for the 2026-27 academic year. Fees vary based on institution type, location, and language version, with Dhaka's non-MPO colleges charging the most.
details: The Ministry of Education has determined session charges and admission fees for Class 11 enrollment in the 2026-27 academic year, ranging from a maximum of Tk 8,500 to a minimum of Tk 1,500.

The highest fee, Tk 8,500, will be applicable to non-MPO or partially MPO colleges in the Dhaka Metropolitan area. Fees are also differentiated based on whether the institution is MPO-listed, its geographical location, and whether it offers Bangla or English versions.

This information was revealed from the Class 11 admission policy published by the Secondary and Higher Education Division of the Ministry of Education on Monday, August 24, 2026. This year, the education board will charge an application fee of Tk 340, an increase of Tk 5 from last year's Tk 335.

For MPO-listed colleges, the admission fee is Tk 5,000 in Dhaka Metropolitan areas (for both Bangla and English versions). In other metropolitan areas, the fee is Tk 3,000, while in districts it is Tk 2,000 (Bangla and English versions). For upazilas and rural areas, the fee is Tk 1,500.

For non-MPO colleges in Dhaka Metropolitan, the fee is Tk 7,500 for the Bangla version and Tk 8,500 for the English version. In other metropolitan areas, Bangla version costs Tk 5,000 and English version costs Tk 6,000.

In districts, non-MPO colleges will charge Tk 3,000 for the Bangla version and Tk 4,000 for the English version. For upazilas and rural areas, the admission fees are Tk 2,500 for Bangla and Tk 3,000 for English versions.

The education board will collect a total of Tk 340 from students during the initial admission confirmation. This includes Tk 142 for registration, Tk 50 for sports, Tk 15 for Rover/Ranger, Tk 16 for Red Crescent, Tk 7 for science and technology, Tk 10 for BNCC, and Tk 100 for teacher welfare and retirement benefits.

Additionally, an online application fee of Tk 220 has been set for Class 11 admissions. Each student is also required to send Tk 24 for the Red Crescent fee and Tk 400 for the annual sports grant to the board.

headline: Gold prices rise again in Bangladesh, 22K gold hits 247,743 BDT
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has announced a price hike of up to 1,633 BDT per bhori for the highest quality gold.
details: Gold prices in the domestic market have increased once again. The highest quality or 22-carat gold has seen a price hike of up to 1,633 BDT per bhori.
caption:
